what: TG Therapeutics sells Briumvi, an infused antibody treatment for relapsing multiple sclerosis, and is developing a version patients can inject themselves.
customers: Neurologists treating multiple sclerosis, paid for by insurers and Medicare.
money: royalties from partners outside the United States
moat: An approved drug in a category where the alternatives are dominant and expensive, with an infusion time shorter than the market leader's, which neurologists and infusion centres value.
risks: 97 times earnings: the price assumes years of continued launch growth
A single product provides essentially all revenue
Roche's Ocrevus dominates the category and is launching its own subcutaneous version
opportunities: Revenue grew from $234M to $616M in two years and is $898M over the last twelve months
A 72.6% gross-level margin, typical of a specialty biologic
A subcutaneous version in development would let patients inject at home instead of attending an infusion centre
watch: Briumvi prescription growth and progress on the subcutaneous formulation.
